AnswerRequest.description: An answer to a question. Fill in the one field that matches the question's form.
AnswerRequest.title: AnswerRequest

Ask.description: A question the learner asked about a part of a lesson, and the answer.
Ask.title: Ask

AskPicture.description: The part's picture, drawn again because the learner asked (ADR-067).
AskPicture.title: AskPicture

AskRequest.description: Something the learner wants to ask about one part of a lesson.
AskRequest.title: AskRequest

Beat.description: One breath of narration, and what appears on screen as it starts.
Beat.title: Beat

CoreSettings.description: What the core keeps of the learner's settings, as a file holds it.
CoreSettings.title: CoreSettings

CourseFileHolds.description: What goes into a file, or is brought in from one. The curriculum always is.
CourseFileHolds.title: CourseFileHolds

CourseFileSummary.description: What a file says it is, for asking the learner before anything is brought in.
CourseFileSummary.title: CourseFileSummary

ExplanationSegment.description: Narration with key points on the board, and optionally a scene beside it.
ExplanationSegment.title: ExplanationSegment

FilmMakerStatus.description: Whether the film maker is on this computer, and what setting it up takes.
FilmMakerStatus.title: FilmMakerStatus

FilmPlanOut.description: What a film of the course would be, before it is begun or continued.
FilmPlanOut.title: FilmPlanOut

FilmVideoPart.description: A part of a film's video, for the page to put together and play.
FilmVideoPart.title: FilmVideoPart

Hypothesis.description: A possible explanation for a pattern of answers. A hypothesis, never a verdict.
Hypothesis.title: Hypothesis

ImportRequest.description: Absolute paths chosen by the learner. Only the desktop shell may send this.
ImportRequest.title: ImportRequest

InteractionSegment.description: A scene the learner manipulates. Understandable without touching it.
InteractionSegment.title: InteractionSegment

JobProgressDetail.description:
What long work is doing just now, for a learner who is waiting for it.

Nothing here is the answer itself: a stage, and the titles of what has been written.
JobProgressDetail.title: JobProgressDetail

Knowledge.description: What the evidence says about the learner and one concept. Deliberately no score.
Knowledge.title: Knowledge

LessonAuthor.description: Who wrote a lesson, by the names they went by when it was written.
LessonAuthor.title: LessonAuthor

LessonForPlayer.description: Everything the player needs: the validated lesson and the scenes it plays.
LessonForPlayer.title: LessonForPlayer

LessonRequest.description: How the learner would like a new lesson to teach, when they have a preference.
LessonRequest.title: LessonRequest

LessonRules.description:
How Adle forms a lesson (ADR-061): the rules of every lesson, in the order a lesson
obeys them, and what each subject needs besides.
LessonRules.title: LessonRules

Narration.description: What of a lesson has been recorded in the voice chosen now, and the recording under way.
Narration.title: Narration

NextStep.description: Something worth doing now, with the reason for it. Never an instruction.
NextStep.title: NextStep

PlayerQuestion.description: A question as the learner sees it before answering.
PlayerQuestion.title: PlayerQuestion

ProgressSummary.description: Counts of concepts by what the evidence says. Counts of states, never a score.
ProgressSummary.title: ProgressSummary

ProposalAcceptance.description: Which concepts of a proposal to add, by their position in it.
ProposalAcceptance.title: ProposalAcceptance

ProviderRoute.description: Where one kind of request would go at this moment, and how long it may take.
ProviderRoute.title: ProviderRoute

ProviderRoutes.description: Where each kind of request would go. Read just before saying where one will go.
ProviderRoutes.title: ProviderRoutes

ProviderStatus.description: The learner's choice, every provider there is, and where requests would go.
ProviderStatus.title: ProviderStatus

ProviderUsage.description:
Adle's own count of today's requests to one provider.

An estimate: the provider keeps the real one.
ProviderUsage.title: ProviderUsage

ReflectionSegment.description: A question to think about. Not scored; the learner may write a note or move on.
ReflectionSegment.title: ReflectionSegment

SavedFilmFile.description: A film written for the desktop shell to move where the learner chose.
SavedFilmFile.title: SavedFilmFile

SceneArtifact.description: One complete Wanim scene file, with what the static policy found in it.
SceneArtifact.title: SceneArtifact

SceneTrial.description: A picture to try in the player before a learner is shown it (ADR-038).
SceneTrial.title: SceneTrial

SceneTrialReport.description: How a trial went. ``passed``, or where it failed and what the player said.
SceneTrialReport.title: SceneTrialReport

SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

SourceCitation.description: A place in the learner's materials that the lesson draws on.
SourceCitation.title: SourceCitation

SubjectWay.description: One kind of subject, and how a lesson of it goes.
SubjectWay.title: SubjectWay

SummarySegment.description: The key points, shown on the board or in a picture that brings them back (ADR-049).
SummarySegment.title: SummarySegment

UnhelpfulReport.description: The learner says a part of a lesson did not help.
UnhelpfulReport.title: UnhelpfulReport

VoiceDescription.description: The description a voice of some parts is made from.
VoiceDescription.title: VoiceDescription

VoiceDesignPart.description: One thing about a voice a learner can choose: who speaks, how fast, and so on.
VoiceDesignPart.title: VoiceDesignPart

VoiceDesignPreset.description: A voice to start from: a choice of parts, and the description they make.
VoiceDesignPreset.title: VoiceDesignPreset

VoicePlan.description: What bringing a file's voice in would do on this computer.
VoicePlan.title: VoicePlan

VoiceRecording.description: A lesson being recorded in the voice chosen now (ADR-057).
VoiceRecording.title: VoiceRecording

VoiceSampleRequest.description:
A few words in a voice set up here: a speaker of a size, or the Expressive voice of a
description or of parts (the one chosen when neither is given).
VoiceSampleRequest.title: VoiceSampleRequest

VoiceTier.description: One size of natural voice, from the lightest (Kokoro) to the richest (Qwen3-TTS 1.7B).
VoiceTier.title: VoiceTier

WorkedExampleSegment.description:
A problem solved step by step: each beat says a step and shows it, on the board or
in its picture (a slide that grows with the solution, ADR-049).
WorkedExampleSegment.title: WorkedExampleSegment

WrittenBy.description: Who wrote something a model wrote.
WrittenBy.title: WrittenBy

post.description: The learner says a suspected mistake does not describe them.
Start writing a lesson. The body is optional: without it Adle chooses how to teach.
Questions worth asking about a concept now. May be empty; the reason says why.
Add the sample course that ships with Adle, or return it if it is already there.

parameters.description: Record that the learner opened the course.
parameters.name: opened

schema.description: Record that the learner opened the course.
schema.title: Opened

get.description: The newest proposal for a course, so one that finished unseen can still be reviewed.

post.description: Begin the course's film, or continue it where it was left.

get.description: Work still in progress for a course, so a screen can pick it up again after navigating.
The suggested next step with its reason, the alternatives, and where each concept stands.

post.description: Set the film maker up: it is downloaded, at the learner's word (ADR-065).

get.description:
Films being made, and the film maker being set up, in any course: for the app to
say so wherever the learner is, and that a film is ready when it is.

post.description: Write a film, and its subtitles, where the desktop shell collects them.

get.description: Liveness check used by the desktop shell after the ready handshake.

Lessons and lists of concepts being written, in any course.

So that the app can say, wherever the learner is, that something is on its way.

How a lesson is formed: said to the learner as it is said to a lesson's writer,
from the one place it is written down (``lessons/axioms.py``).
Everything the learner has asked about this lesson, oldest first.

post.description:
Ask Adle something about one part of a lesson. The answer is written by a model.

Starts a job and returns at once. When it has finished, the answer is among
``lessons.list_asks``.

delete.description:
Give the part its own picture back, in place of the one an answer drew. The lesson
as it is now, to be played.

post.description:
Put the picture an answer drew into its part of the lesson, in place of the part's
own (ADR-067). The lesson as it is now, to be played.
Score an answer, keep it, and record it as evidence about the concept.
The learner says an explanation did not help. It shapes what is suggested next.

delete.description: The learner takes back "this did not help" about a part: it was said by mistake.

post.description:
Ask one provider for one word, to find out whether its key works.

It counts as one request there. Nothing of the learner's is sent.

put.description:
Record the learner's choice: one provider, or every one they have a key for.

No key is touched. Refused while something is being written.

get.description: Today's count at one provider: the one named, or the one a lesson would go to.

Pictures to try in the player before a learner is shown them (ADR-038).

The app asks while a lesson is being written; asking is also how it says that it is
there to try them.

post.description: How a trial went. A report nobody is waiting for any more is let go.
What a file's voice would be on this computer. Nothing is changed.
Read the pages of a file that are pictures, at the learner's word (ADR-060).

The description a voice of these parts is made from (ADR-062): written by the core,
so that the same parts are always the same voice. Nothing is changed.
A sample of a voice, made in the background, once (ADR-057): the job's result names it.
Set a size of voice up: it is downloaded, at the learner's word (ADR-042).
